newsitem.title: EGYPT: Strong storm hits Egypt, disrupts air traffic.
newsitem.headline: Strong storm hits Egypt, disrupts air traffic.

text.p: A strong sandstorm hit the Egyptian capital on Friday and disrupted air traffic at Cairo International Airport, Egyptian officials said.

"The storm has blown at a speed of 110 km (68 miles) per hour. The country has not witnessed such a strong storm for 30 years at least," Abdul Moneim Abdul Rahman, chairman of the Meteorological Authority, told Reuters.
International and domestic flights were diverted to other aiports in the country but normal air traffic resumed at Cairo airport about 90 minutes later, airport sources said.
The storm blowing from the Western Desert reduced visibility to less than 50 metres (165 feet) in the afternoon, Abdul Rahman said.
A number of people were slightly injured when advertisement billboards outside Cairo airport fell down, airport sources said.
Officials at the Interior Ministry told Reuters that it had only received reports on the storm knocking down several trees.
Egypt usually suffers from sandstorms at this time of the year. They are called Khamasin (fifty) because they blow intermittently for about 50 days.
